column1: # Per-sample reference standard for ENA study PRJEB30781, transcribed from Tables 1 and 2 of the
#   Charalampous T, Kay GL, Richardson H, Aydin A, Baldan R, Jeanes C, Rae D, Grundy S, Turner DJ,
#   Wain J, Leggett RM, Livermore DM, O'Grady J (2019): "Nanopore metagenomics enables rapid
#   clinical diagnosis of bacterial lower respiratory infection." Nat Biotechnol 37(7):783-792.
# `culture' is the routine microbiology result, `wimp' what that study's own pipeline (ONT WIMP,
# k-mer based) reported. NRF = normal respiratory flora, NSG = no significant growth, None = the
# pipeline reported no pathogen. Several samples carry more than one organism
# THIS IS A SAMPLE-LEVEL STANDARD, NOT A READ-LEVEL ONE: sigma is the organism the sample contains,
# not the species a single read stems from. The per-read averages of Section "Measuring classification
# quality" therefore cannot be formed from it. The candidate precision q of that section can, since it
# needs sigma only where a call is made: for a call k it is 1/|Sigma(k)| if the reference organism lies
# in Sigma(k), and 0 otherwise. That is what the two taxid columns are for. Note also that culture is a demonstrably incomplete standard here: the
# study's specificity against it was 41.7 %, and most of its apparent false positives were
# The last two columns give the NCBI taxid of the organism named in `culture' and in `wimp', resolved
# against data/common/names.dmp. They are empty where the entry names no species: NRF, NSG, None and
# `Coliform', which is a group rather than a taxon. Two entries needed a decision. MRSA is
# Staphylococcus aureus (1280) -- the resistance is not a taxon of its own. E. aerogenes is today
# Klebsiella aerogenes (548), which is the name the taxonomy carries. The abbreviations stay as
# transcribed, because they are what the paper prints
